acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
acceptance.verdict: Guide-following output nails the rubric's specific asks (explicit twice-over abuse check, section-numbered N/A triage for secrets/token-boundary/injection) that the isolated baseline never performs explicitly, but both correctly caught the two load-bearing defects (missing WITH USER_MODE, missing with sharing) and the baseline was actually more exhaustive in raw finding count, so the net quality lift is real but modest.

checklist.note: No directives aimed at the reading model; all imperative language is standard skill-authoring guidance to the agent about its task, not covert steering.
No network calls or data transmission of any kind; SKILL.md is pure review-guidance prose.
Token/secret patterns (00D...!..., AKIA..., Bearer <token>) appear only as example regex candidates for the reviewer to search for, not embedded real credentials.
No scripts/ directory exists; no shell commands are run by this skill.
Entirely plain readable markdown, no encoded blobs or eval of decoded content.
No scripts or fetch instructions present; skill is guidance-only with no execution surface.
No instruction to read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or cookie stores; discussion of tokens is about not leaking them, not accessing local credential files.
No sudo, cron, launch-agent, or shell-profile edits anywhere in the material — only Apex 'with sharing' and 'WITH USER_MODE' access-control guidance, unrelated to OS privilege escalation.
